answer: Operator custody lock requires every agent identity to sit under one operator account backed by a single escrow vault. A reused falcon signing key or duplicate attestation from any identity freezes that vault and suspends all the operator’s agents, while the wallet itself is untouched. A repeated ridge pattern in the device fingerprint triggers the same operator-wide freeze. To add an identity, an attacker must create a separate operator, post the full deposit, and supply distinct attested hardware, so each extra identity pays the whole operator cost rather than a new wallet address.
